summary: Clarify per-key vs tenant rate limits and recommend client-side backoff strategy
description: Issue summary: BrightCart reports sporadic 429 responses across multiple API keys after migrating to a dedicated pool. They see rapid 429 bursts when ramping many short-lived connections from their client fleet. Request: clarify which limits are enforced per API key vs per-tenant/dedicated-pool and provide recommended client-side backoff/connection strategies for mixed streaming and short-polling workloads. Impact: customer-facing recommendations and potential config changes; currently affecting search-related features (approx 3% error rate) during traffic spikes.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Multiple service instances (kubectl scale replicas=50) each open short-lived POST /v1/chat/completions requests with max_tokens=256 and a few long-poll streaming requests.
2) Use 10 distinct API keys scoped to a single BrightCart account (tenant) with Dedicated pool in us-east.
3) Ramp to ~1200 requests/min over 2 minutes.
4) Observe 429s returned intermittently from the gateway and occasional 502 during backend fallback.
Notes: customer reports higher error rates when using multiplexed websocket connections from a single host versus distributing keys across hosts.
logs_and_evidence:
Gateway log excerpt (trimmed):
[2026-03-12T13:41:02Z] INFO request start key=key_01 tenant=brightcart region=us-east endpoint=/v1/chat status=200 latency_ms=120
[2026-03-12T13:41:10Z] WARN quota_check key=key_07 tenant=brightcart reason=burst_limit_exceeded status=429
[2026-03-12T13:41:11Z] WARN quota_check key=key_03 tenant=brightcart reason=burst_limit_exceeded status=429
[2026-03-12T13:41:12Z] ERROR upstream_fallback tenant=brightcart region=us-east to_model=redwood/gpt-4o-instruct-32k result=502
Customer supplied client logs: multiple clients log HTTP 429 with X-RateLimit-Reset header ~3s and X-Redwood-Quota-Bucket=tenant:shared_az1.
Relevant dashboards: link to internal grafana panel (support-only): https://grafana.redwood.company/d/xyz/rate-limiter?orgId=1
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: Dedicated pools enforce both per-API-key smoothing buckets and a tenant-wide burst guard; rapid short requests across many keys can trigger tenant-level guards causing uneven 429s. Verified via sampling logs: tenant-level 'shared_az1' bucket reached burst threshold at 2026-03-12T13:41:10Z.
Findings: 1) Per-key token buckets exist for steady-state QPS limits. 2) Tenant/dedicated-pool burst guard exists to protect the serving runtime from sudden fan-out spikes. 3) Multiplexing from a single host concentrated requests into the same upstream connection and sometimes hit connection-based limits at the gateway leading to backpressure behavior.
Next steps: engineering to confirm exact burst thresholds for dedicated pools (INT-872 opened to track config audit). Recommend client configuration changes while we confirm thresholds.
recommended_workarounds:
1) Distribute API keys across hosts (avoid single-host multiplexing of many keys). 2) Implement exponential backoff with jitter for 429s (initial retry after X-RateLimit-Reset or default 500ms, then multiply by 1.5-2.0 with randomized jitter). 3) Use connection pooling for streaming clients: prefer long-lived streaming connections per key rather than many short streaming opens. 4) If predictable throughput required, consider BrightCart increasing Dedicated pool capacity or configuring Reserved burst for time windows. 5) For immediate mitigation, enable client-side token-bucket pacing: cap per-host concurrent requests to 8 when ramping.
Suggested backoff pseudo-policy: on 429 -> wait header X-RateLimit-Reset if present (ceil to ms) else wait 500-800ms; retry up to 3 times with multiplier 1.6 and random jitter +/-20%.
resolution_notes: Pending. Partial mitigation validated: customer applied client-side host-level concurrency cap and jittered backoff; observed 75% reduction in 429 rate in next ramp test. Engineering (INT-872) to confirm whether we should raise tenant burst guard for this dedicated pool or add config knobs for ReservedBurst windows. Plan: coordinate with BrightCart for a controlled capacity increase next week if config change is not desirable.
